items.title: FDIC proposes giving interstate state banks the same host-state-law treatment as national banks
items.summary: The FDIC proposes applying a host state’s laws to an out-of-state state-chartered bank only to the same extent those laws apply to an out-of-state national bank, whether services are delivered through a branch or without one. Where host-state law does not apply to the national bank, the state bank would receive the same treatment. The proposal does not itself decide whether any particular state law is federally preempted; comments close November 23.

items.title: Energy Department proposes clearer deadlines for contractor-retaliation proceedings
items.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Hearings and Appeals
items.summary: The Department of Energy proposes revising the procedures used when contractor employees allege retaliation by their employers. The changes would clarify deadlines and when those periods are tolled, update references to responsible officials and offices, and make consistency edits across the Contractor Employee Protection Program. The proposal concerns adjudicative procedure rather than the merits of any employee’s claim. Public comments are due October 22, 2026.

items.title: FDA replaces animal-testing language with broader nonclinical-testing terminology
items.summary: FDA issued a direct final rule replacing selected references to “animal” or “preclinical” tests with “nonclinical” terminology and defining nonclinical tests and studies. The agency says the amendments add no requirements, align the regulations with recent statutory changes, and remove wording that treats animal testing as the only safety-assessment method. The rule is scheduled for February 4, 2027, but FDA will withdraw it if significant adverse comments arrive by December 7.

items.title: Census proposes sharing protected business data with BEA for statistical work
items.summary: The Census Bureau proposes sharing certain business data with the Bureau of Economic Analysis under the Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency Act. That statute permits designated statistical agencies to exchange identifiable business information for statistical purposes, subject to its confidentiality regime. The notice therefore concerns the legal boundary between protected firm-level records and interagency production of economic statistics; it does not announce public release of identifiable records. Comments are due November 23.

items.title: FDIC proposes faster bank-merger review and deemed approval for qualifying small transactions
items.summary: The FDIC proposes a new Bank Merger Act framework with a 21-day completeness determination, tailored processing tracks, and “deemed approval” for qualifying de minimis transactions. Its initial competition screen would count credit-union shares and centrally booked deposits, while some small deals would lose their public-comment period. The proposal would also codify standards now partly embedded in internal practice. These are proposed changes, not current approval rules; comments are due November 23.

items.title: Maritime Administration proposes broadening tax-deferred vessel construction accounts
items.summary: The Maritime Administration proposes updating the Capital Construction Fund program to cover all U.S.-built vessels engaged in domestic or foreign commerce, implementing recent statutory amendments and removing older geographic-trade limits. The rule would clarify reconstruction deadlines, permit account funds to support acquisitions in specified circumstances, and create a process to terminate zero-balance, inactive, or unstarted accounts after ten years. The proposal could alter how vessel owners defer income for fleet investment; comments close November 23.

items.title: NOAA proposes immediate South Atlantic black sea bass limits while reassessing the stock
items.summary: NOAA proposes commercial and recreational catch targets below existing limits, a lower recreational bag limit, and a February–March spawning closure for South Atlantic black sea bass. A 2025 assessment update found the stock overfished and undergoing overfishing, but managers are revising inputs including recreational catch estimates before setting longer-term policy. The interim proposal responds to continuing declines in biomass, abundance, survey indices, and landings while that methodological dispute remains unresolved.

items.title: Executive order directs agencies to expand hunting access, game management, and venison donation
items.summary: Executive Order 14429 directs federal agencies to identify more hunting opportunities for youth and veterans, coordinate habitat and game-population management, and support state venison-donation programs for schools and food banks. Its listed tools include prescribed fire, grazing, predator management, invasive-species control, and voluntary agreements with landowners. The order was signed September 17 and published September 22; implementation remains subject to existing legal authority and appropriations, and the order creates no privately enforceable right.

items.title: Pentagon publishes proposed $686 million Pakistan F-16 modernization sale
items.summary: A Defense Department notification describes a proposed $686 million sale to Pakistan comprising 92 Link-16 systems, six inert bomb bodies, cryptographic and identification equipment, software, training, spares, and support for F-16 modernization. The agency says refurbishment would extend the fleet’s service life through 2040 and preserve interoperability; those are the department’s stated justifications, not independent findings. The underlying notice was delivered to Congress on December 4, 2025, but published now in the Federal Register.

items.title: FAA proposes replacing cracked Airbus A300 landing-gear components
items.summary: The FAA proposes requiring replacement of affected main landing gear on several Airbus A300 variants after incorrectly machined two-piece cages developed cracks. The agency says uncorrected cracking could produce landing-gear structural failure during takeoff or landing. Ninety-nine U.S.-registered aircraft would fall within the proposal; the FAA estimates $235,620 in fleetwide labor but lacks data for replacement-part costs. The measure incorporates a 2025 European Union Aviation Safety Agency directive and remains open for comment through November 6.

items.title: FAA proposes early replacement of Airbus A350 fuel-control units after stiction reports
items.summary: The FAA proposes shortened life limits and replacement of specified hydro-mechanical units on certain Airbus A350-941 aircraft. Engine monitoring traced abnormal behavior to wear-induced stiction in a spill valve, which could cause an internal fuel leak and reduced thrust under high power demand; with loss of the other engine, control could be impaired. The proposal covers 38 U.S.-registered aircraft and estimates maximum fleet costs of about $79.2 million. Comments are due November 6.

items.title: NHTSA seeks comment on alternative spine and face designs for an advanced crash dummy
items.summary: NHTSA supplemented its 2023 proposal to add the THOR-50M, an advanced 50th-percentile adult male crash-test dummy, to federal regulations. The new notice asks for comment on an additional spine configuration and an alternative face foam and makes supporting technical documents available. It does not yet adopt the device or revise a vehicle-safety standard. The narrow proposal is useful as a view into how measurement hardware itself becomes standardized before it can govern comparative crash testing.

items.title: Opt-out screening found newly identified syphilis in 2.2% of people tested in Alaska corrections
items.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
items.summary: Among 5,163 adults screened in Alaska correctional facilities during October 2023–September 2025, 4.6% had reactive rapid plasma reagin tests and 2.2% had newly identified syphilis; 77.2% of the newly identified group completed treatment. Reactive results were more frequent among women tested (9.3%) than men (3.5%). This was public-health surveillance, not a randomized study, and the authors lacked complete data on people who opted out or left custody before routine intake.

items.title: Emergency visits for heat illness rose sharply across four U.S. regions during a ten-day heat dome
items.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
items.summary: CDC syndromic-surveillance data show that heat-related emergency-department visit rates during June 28–July 7, 2026 were markedly above rates for the same dates in earlier years across eastern, midwestern, southern, and south-central regions. Rates peaked around the July 4 holiday. The report links the timing to a persistent heat dome but describes surveillance associations rather than estimating the event’s complete causal mortality or morbidity burden. It emphasizes rapid monitoring as a basis for targeted warnings and response.

items.title: Congo’s 2026 Ebola outbreak grew faster in its first 100 days than four historical outbreaks
items.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
items.geography: Democratic Republic of the Congo / Uganda
items.summary: CDC’s comparative surveillance report records 5,458 confirmed cases and 2,606 deaths during the first 100 days of the 2026 Bundibugyo-virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. That is seven times the case count reported over the corresponding period of the 2014 West African outbreak, previously the largest overall. Historical case definitions differ, and this was an operational public-health analysis rather than research, but the trajectory supports the report’s conclusion that transmission was expanding exceptionally quickly.
